device.description: 16-bit multiplying-optimized voltage-output DAC with 24-bit SPI-compatible write-only interface and VFB feedback pin
device.note: dac8501.pdf (SBAS212A) p.2 pin description, p.3 electrical characteristics (VDD 2.7-5.5 V, logic inputs), p.4 timing characteristics and serial write operation, p.12 serial interface, input shift register (Figure 3) and SYNC interrupt (Figure 4), p.13 power-on reset to zero and power-down modes (Table I)

registers.name: DAC
registers.note: DAC register; power-on reset fills it with zeros (p.13)

registers.name: CTRL
registers.note: internal: PD1/PD0 (DB17-DB16) of the last valid frame: 00 normal, 01 1 kOhm, 10 100 kOhm, 11 Hi-Z

commands.name: WRITE
commands.note: DB23-DB18 don't care, DB17-DB16 PD1/PD0, DB15-DB0 data MSB first; executed on the 24th SCLK falling edge; SYNC high earlier aborts the frame (SYNC interrupt)

pages: p.2 (pins), p.3 (specifications, VDD 2.7-5.5 V), p.4 (timing), p.12 (serial interface, input shift register Figure 3, SYNC interrupt), p.13 (power-on reset, power-down Table I)
notModeled: analog output, resistor string, output amplifier and VFB feedback input (VOUT is never driven)
power-down output loads (1 kOhm / 100 kOhm / Hi-Z): PD1/PD0 stored in CTRL.PD only; the DAC register keeps its contents
power-down exit time (2.5 us at 5 V, 5 us at 3 V) and output settling
SCLK frequency (20 MHz below VDD 3.6 V, 30 MHz above) and setup/hold limits t1-t8
SPI mode: data taken on SCLK falling edges, SCLK high at SYNC fall in the timing figure; modeled as mode 2
multiplying-mode behavior: the resistor string keeps drawing reference current in power-down (analog)
variants: dac8501.pdf covers only the DAC8501 (a DAC8531 optimized for multiplying mode; same pinout and frame, own spec file DAC8531).
